explanations: The encoder turns any dataclass into a dict with dataclasses.asdict, which recursively includes every field. get_trip and request_ride return a Trip whose driver is a Driver dataclass containing phone and payout_account, so those private fields are sent to the rider in every trip response. Serialization of rider-facing data should go through an explicit view or whitelist of public driver fields (display name, plate, rating) rather than a generic dump of the model.

DispatchEncoder.default returns str(o) for Decimal, so the value is a JSON string that preserves the exact digits and scale. A JSON number would need float conversion, which is not done. There is no structured Decimal representation, and Decimal is explicitly handled, so no TypeError occurs.

fromisoformat parses the string successfully into a naive datetime, then parse_ride_request explicitly rejects naive values with a RequestError, which request_ride maps to 400. No timezone is assumed, and since the request is rejected before dispatch, the encoder's naive-datetime TypeError is never reached.

In Python bool is a subclass of int, so isinstance(True, int) is true; the explicit isinstance(seats, bool) test is what rejects it, producing a RequestError and a 400. Without that test it would be accepted as 1, and nothing in this path raises an unhandled exception.
